newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares climb higher but seen cooling.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares climb higher but seen cooling.

text.p: Bullish Chilean shares extended their New Year's rally on continued strong demand from abroad, shrugging off comments by the Central Bank chief that there would be no immediate cut in interest rates.

Volume held relatively brisk, suggesting rises were on strong footing, but some brokers said it was time for the bourse to take a breather and that shares would probably level off Wednesday, especially since some selling began late Tuesday.
"It's not unusual for shares to rise four sessions in a row after falling for the previous three months," said one.
The blue-chip IPSA index ended 1.41 percent higher for the day at 107.26 points. The all-share IGPA rose 0.92 percent to 5098.06 points on volume of 20.6 billion pesos, or 122 million shares traded.

The market paid little heed to statements by Central Bank President Carlos Massad, who said he expected no immediate cut in interest rates, although some kind of relaxation in monetary policies would come later.
Risers included Laboratorio Chile, up 6.3 percent to 372 pesos, and electrical shares, which often set the tone for the market.
Endesa rose two percent to 231 pesos and Chilgener, which has announced a series of expansion plans, was up 0.2 percent to 2,305 pesos.
Decliners included Soquimich A shares, off one percent to 2,000 pesos, and Entel, down 1.3 percent to 2,940 pesos.
